note_on_method: Each venue page rests on one line of the City of St. George's Pickleball page, a name, a street address and a court count under the heading "City of St. George Pickleball Courts", plus, for Little Valley, the 2025 programme schedule, the check-in rule and the 2020 article on the same page, and, for Vernon Worthen, one sentence of that article about where the programme began. The US Census address geocoder supplies the county and the postcode. Where the City is silent, these pages record the silence.

slots.description:
Thirty-three pickleball courts at the City's Little Valley complex, tied for the largest single-venue count on this site and the first venue here published as a dedicated pickleball facility.

The City's line is "Little Valley / 2149 Horseman Park Drive / Courts:  33", and the page heads the venue "Little Valley Pickleball Complex". This is a programmed facility rather than a park with courts in it: the same page carries the City's 2025 schedule, which numbers the courts, reserves "9-32 (24 courts)" for league sessions, and books "All 33 Courts" for two tournaments a year.

The City's 2020 article says the complex was then "home to 24 well-maintained courts". The article is dated 19 August 2020; the list is the City's undated present. So thirty-three publishes, and twenty-four is what the venue was.
slots.getting_there:
2149 Horseman Park Drive, St. George, UT 84790. The US Census address geocoder matched the address at house-number level and placed it in Washington County, in the incorporated place St. George city. The Census file spells the street "HORESMAN PARK DR", a transposition, and the City's spelling is the one published here.

The City publishes nothing about parking at the complex, and nothing about restrooms. What it does say about arriving is a rule: "Players, please check in with the attendant or instructor to determine if courts are available during the St. George Pickleball programs".
slots.what_to_expect:
A facility with an attendant, a timetable and a numbered court plan. During the City's programmes, courts 9 to 32 are reserved for league play on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday mornings and evenings, and the Rock N Roll Tournament in February and the Southern Shootout in April take all thirty-three courts from 8:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m.

The City takes court reservations through the Parks Department at 435-627-4530. Non-City events need a reservation and possibly a special event permit, displayed on the court.

Nothing is stated about lighting, surface, opening hours or whether any court is covered.

faqs.a: When the courts are vacant, yes. The City's 2020 article says "When courts are vacant the public readily takes advantage of them", and adds "free of charge". During City programmes, courts are reserved and an attendant says what is available.
Not stated. The City schedules league play until 9:30 p.m. on winter evenings but never uses the word lights, and this site records lighting only when the operator states it.

slots.description:
Six pickleball courts at Vernon Worthen Park, the place where the City of St. George's pickleball programme began.

The City's line is "Vernon Worthen / 300 S. 400 E. / Courts: 6", the smallest count of the three published venues. The City's 2020 article supplies the history: "In 2012, Wayne Bullock established the first pickleball program for the City of St. George on four permanent and two temporary courts at Vernon Worthen Park."

So the park has two counts in the City's record: four permanent and two temporary in 2012, and six on the undated current list. An origin is not an inventory, and this page prints both rather than choosing.
slots.getting_there:
300 S. 400 E., St. George, UT 84770. That is a Utah grid address, 300 South and 400 East, and the US Census address geocoder resolved it as written, "300 S 400 E, ST GEORGE, UT, 84770", at house-number level, in Washington County and in the incorporated place St. George city.

The imported record carried "200 South 400 East", a block away, under the name "Worthen Park"; the City's own line and the City's own name replaced both. The City publishes nothing about parking or restrooms at this park, and no hours.
slots.what_to_expect:
Six courts and no published programme. Everything the City schedules on its pickleball page, leagues, youth sessions, clinics and tournaments, is on a timetable headed Little Valley, and that timetable names no other venue, so nothing on it reserves a court here.

That does not make the courts free: the City's "free of charge" sentence is about Little Valley, and the price at Vernon Worthen is not stated. The City also states no hours, no lighting, no surface, and nothing about whether the six courts are dedicated or share ground with tennis.

Six courts is six doubles games, twenty-four players on court before anyone waits, which is a workable drop-in number without being a complex.

faqs.a: Six, on the City's current list: "Vernon Worthen / 300 S. 400 E. / Courts: 6". The imported record said seven; the City's figure replaced it.
Not stated. The City's "free of charge" sentence is about Little Valley. Nothing is published about the price here, so it is recorded as unknown rather than free.

slots.description:
Seven pickleball courts at Bloomington Park in the south-west of St. George, the second-largest count of the three published venues in the city.

The City's whole record of this venue is one line: "Bloomington Park / 650 Man O War Road / Courts: 7". It sits third in the four-line list headed "City of St. George Pickleball Courts", between Vernon Worthen's six and the four at Ledges that cannot be published for want of an address. Seven is an odd number for a block of courts, and the City does not say how they are laid out, whether they were built as pickleball courts, or whether any share a slab with tennis.

Nothing else on the City's page names this park. The 2020 article, the programme schedule, the check-in rule and the free-of-charge sentence all belong to Little Valley.
slots.getting_there:
650 Man O War Road, St. George, UT 84790. The US Census address geocoder matched "650 MAN O WAR RD, ST GEORGE, UT, 84790" at house-number level and placed it in Washington County, in the incorporated place St. George city.

The imported dataset held a row for this park with the city written "Saint George", which is not how the City writes it, so this entry was created from the City's own line. The City publishes nothing about parking, restrooms or hours at this park.
slots.what_to_expect:
Seven courts, and no other stated fact about them. The City publishes no price for Bloomington Park, since the "free of charge" sentence on its page is about Little Valley, so the fee is recorded as unknown rather than as free. It publishes no hours and no lighting, so there is no stated evening window. It publishes no surface, and it never calls the courts indoor or outdoor.

It schedules nothing here either: every league, clinic and tournament on the City's 2025 programme is timetabled at Little Valley.

Seven courts is seven doubles games at once, twenty-eight people on court before a queue forms.

faqs.a: Seven, on the City's list: "Bloomington Park / 650 Man O War Road / Courts: 7". The City does not say how they are laid out.
Not stated. The City's pickleball page gives this park a name, an address and a count, and no amenity list.

sources.evidence: The City's Pickleball page. Under "City of St. George Pickleball Courts" exactly four lines: "Little Valley / 2149 Horseman Park Drive / Courts:  33", "Vernon Worthen / 300 S. 400 E. / Courts: 6", "Bloomington Park / 650 Man O War Road / Courts: 7", "Ledges / ? / Courts: 4". The venue heading "Little Valley Pickleball Complex". The check-in rule: "Players, please check in with the attendant or instructor to determine if courts are available during the St. George Pickleball programs". The "St. George Pickleball Program Schedule / 2025", under the heading "Little Valley", reserving "9-32 (24 courts)" for Winter and Spring League sessions, "21-22, 26-29 (6 courts)" for youth sessions, "27-28 (2 courts)" for adult clinics, and "All 33 Courts" from 8:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. for the Rock N Roll Tournament (6-8 February) and the Southern Shootout (2-5 April); "Times may change based on participation numbers". The article dated "St. George, UT, August 19, 2020": chosen as "Public Facility of the Year" by the PPR; "In 2012, Wayne Bullock established the first pickleball program for the City of St. George on four permanent and two temporary courts at Vernon Worthen Park."; "During that time Bullock creatively launched the ladder league format"; "The league format and scorecard became so popular that the USA Pickleball Association contacted Bullock for permission to adopt it."; "The Little Valley Pickleball complex is home to 24 well-maintained courts."; "When courts are vacant the public readily takes advantage of them - free of charge." Also "Please contact Parks to make a court reservation at 435-627-4530", "Non-City events are required to have a court reservation and possibly a special event permit.", "Please display the Court reservation & special event permit on the court.", and a "Reserve a Pickleball Court" link.
